Image 1: Eight-panel storyboard reference, used for the overall shot structure, shot sizes, and camera-movement rhythm. Read it from left to right and from top to bottom; panel N is Shot N. It is a line-art sketch: do not adopt its sketch style, black outlines, white background, panel borders or drawn faces.
Image 2: Reference of JI RAN'S APARTMENT ENTRANCE, the front view, the establishing view, facing the back wall, a rendered set, not live action. Use it only for the room's layout, the furniture's positions and the light's direction; do not reference its visual content. It contains no people.
Image 3: Reference of JI RAN'S APARTMENT ENTRANCE, the back view, turned 180 degrees, facing the front wall, with the left wall at its right edge, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 4: Reference of JI RAN'S APARTMENT ENTRANCE, the left-side view, facing the left wall, with the back wall at its right edge, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 5: Reference of JI RAN'S APARTMENT ENTRANCE, the right-side view, facing the right wall, with the back wall at its left edge, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 6: Reference of JI RAN'S APARTMENT ENTRANCE, the floor plan seen from above: its top edge is the back wall, its bottom edge the front wall behind the front view's camera, and its left and right edges the left and right walls, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 7: Blocking reference of the segment's start: the same place with these people in their places, used only for where each person is and which way they face; take faces and outfits from each subject's own image. It is a line-art diagram: do not adopt its outlines or white background.
Image 8: Subject 1 (Lu Shaoze, look S1) character appearance reference.
Image 9: Subject 2 (Ji Ran, look S3) character appearance reference.
Image 10: Prop 1 (black handbag) maps to this image; copy its writing and badges exactly from Image 10.
From each prop's image, use only structure, material, and color.
[Subject settings]
Subject 1 (Lu Shaoze): Refer to Image 8. 28, Ji Ran's ex-boyfriend of four years, driven off by Ji Hongyuan five years ago and now heir of the Lu Group returning as her arranged-marriage match. Outfit: look S1: Night, returned heir: a tailored navy-blue slim suit jacket over a crisp white open-collar dress shirt, matching navy trousers, polished black oxfords and a silver dress watch. Hair slicked back. Signature colour: blue.
Subject 2 (Ji Ran): Refer to Image 9. 27, Heroine; owner of Jiejian Company, daughter of Ji Hongyuan, and ex-girlfriend of Lu Shaoze. Outfit: look S3: Night, returning home: a fitted ivory satin long-sleeve wrap blouse with a soft V neckline, tucked into a black leather high-waisted mini skirt. Red pointed stiletto heels. She carries the black handbag. Signature colour: red.
Environment (JI RAN'S APARTMENT ENTRANCE): Refer to Images 2 to 6. Night, warm interior downlights with cool elevator spill. Warm ceiling downlights, the soft wall sconce beside the painting and cool light from the open elevator. Quiet lobby hum, an elevator chime, heels on stone.
Do not swap the characters' appearances, clothing, actions, positions or dialogue.
[Overall style]
Photorealistic live-action short drama with cinematic lighting. Each character keeps the face and the outfit with its main colour from their reference image throughout. Use each character sheet only for that character: the face from the close-up on the right, the body and outfit from the turnaround on the left; do not render the sheet's layout, white background or multiple views. This segment has 2 lines, in this order: Lu Shaoze, Ji Ran. Generate speech only from the lines in {} in the shot list, each spoken exactly once by its speaker; everyone else keeps their mouth naturally closed while listening, and a V.O. speaker keeps their mouth closed or is off screen. Follow the shot list below; do not add cuts or camera moves beyond it. Strictly adhere to the 180-degree rule: within a scene, characters keep their screen sides and the camera stays on one side of the axis. Seamless continuity of action, spatial matching and consistent actor blocking; cut on action. For dialogue prefer static shot-reverse-shot and over-the-shoulder shots, balanced with reaction shots and close-up inserts. Faces stable and clear, with no resemblance to any real actor or actress. Normal human eyes. Natural anatomy and hands. Natural, fluid motion that follows the blocking; characters make subtle, natural movements. Characters, props and environment share one world with matched lighting. Each line ends naturally with breathing room and is never cut off. Authentic performances with micro-expressions. No BGM; generate only dialogue, environmental sounds and action sounds. No subtitles.
[Strictly exclude]
subtitles or on-screen text. garbled text on the painting or door. characters crossing sides of the painting. Dialogue from the wrong character, multiple people speaking at once, repeated or missing lines, lip-sync errors and audio-visual desynchronization. The raw reference images (character sheets, setting plates) appearing as a frame of the video, and starting on a still frame of the setting reference. A fast zoom-in at the start, a fast pull-back at the end, unmotivated whip-pans, tilts, zooms and 360-degree orbits. Axis-crossing, jump cuts, frame skips, flicker and clipping. Characters or props popping in or vanishing, and duplicate characters except mirror reflections. Subtitles, captions, watermarks and garbled writing; writing and logos other than those on a key prop's reference image, which are copied from it; a phone screen or paper that is not a key prop is shown from the back or out of focus. Black-and-white, monochrome, grayscale, desaturated visuals; hand-drawn, sketch, line art, illustration, comics, animation; storyboard frames, rough sketches, panel borders, gutters and grid layouts.
[Shot list] (8 shots, approximately 23 seconds)
When a previous-shot reference image is given, it is the moment this segment starts from: keep its people's positions, outfits, props and light, and continue from there. Shot 1 keeps its own camera, matching the image's framing only when it frames the same view; do not repeat that frame later.
At the start: Axis runs along the side wall that holds the one framed autumn landscape painting. That wall stands between the one pair of brushed-steel elevator doors and the one walnut front door with its smart lock, which face each other. The camera stays in front of the painting wall, facing it, for the whole scene. Lu Shaoze, in his navy suit with his hair slicked back, stands at the walnut front door and faces it. The elevator doors behind him are closed. Ji Ran is unseen inside the elevator, in her ivory satin wrap blouse and black leather mini skirt, holding the black handbag. The wall sconce glows beside the painting.
Shot 1 (0-2s): [Wide shot, locked-off camera, eye-level, facing the painting wall, with the walnut front door at frame right and the elevator doors at frame left] Lu Shaoze stands at the walnut front door, smooths his slicked-back hair with one hand and raps on the door with his knuckles. <Three knocks on wood>
Shot 2 (2-4s): [Medium shot, handheld, eye-level, centered on the elevator doors behind Lu Shaoze's back] The elevator doors slide open and cool light spills out. Ji Ran steps out with the black handbag on her arm, her red heels striking the stone floor. <Elevator chime, doors sliding open, heels on stone>
Shot 3 (4-6s): [Medium shot, quick whip pan from the door to the elevator, low angle] Lu Shaoze startles, spins and bumps shoulder-first into Ji Ran. Both stagger and come to a stop beneath the autumn landscape painting, Lu Shaoze at its elevator end and Ji Ran at its front-door end. <Soft thud of a collision>
Shot 4 (6-12s): [Medium shot, over-the-shoulder shot past Ji Ran's shoulder onto Lu Shaoze, eye-level] Lu Shaoze straightens his jacket, then drawls with a smug, lopsided smile, looking her up and down. Dialogue (Lu Shaoze, in Chinese, sneering drawl): {呀，好久不见呀，纪大小姐，您真是贵人事多，这么晚才回家呀。}
Shot 5 (12-13s): [Close-up, locked-off camera, eye-level] Ji Ran rolls her eyes and lifts her chin coolly, her grip settling on the black handbag strap.
Shot 6 (13-18s): [Medium close-up, over-the-shoulder shot past Lu Shaoze's shoulder onto Ji Ran, eye-level] Ji Ran answers with a thin, cutting smile, her head tilted. Dialogue (Ji Ran, in Chinese, deadpan and cutting): {比不上路少爷您清闲，都有空在别人家门口当门神了。}
Shot 7 (18-20s): [Close-up, slow push in on Lu Shaoze's face, eye-level] Lu Shaoze's smile stiffens and one eyebrow twitches. Dialogue (Ji Ran, in Chinese, mocking): {怎么，路少爷这是刚回国，}
Shot 8 (20-23s): [Medium shot, low angle on Ji Ran beneath the painting] Ji Ran glances at the walnut front door behind her, then back at him with a cold smirk. Dialogue (Ji Ran, in Chinese, mocking): {都找不到自己家门口在哪了？}
At the end: Lu Shaoze stands at the elevator end of the autumn landscape painting, facing Ji Ran with a stiffened smile. Ji Ran stands at the front-door end of the painting, facing him with a cold smirk, the black handbag on her arm. The elevator doors have closed behind them. The camera stays in front of the painting wall.
